subject.title: [Bug 6.1] Silent config auto-patch from memory-core + error-message auto-fix breaks all cron jobs on hosts without Docker

question: Should OpenClaw harden assistant/cron-triggered protected config mutation by removing model-visible config-write hints and adding explicit operator provenance or guards for CLI-through-exec config writes?
rationale: The observable current-main gap crosses security posture and persisted user config, and the exact intended boundary between operator CLI guidance and model/cron automation is a maintainer security decision.

options.title: Harden the mutation boundary
options.body: Remove config-write assignments from assistant-visible errors, keep operator-only guidance in explicit CLI/status surfaces, and require audited operator provenance or denial for protected config writes reached through exec/cron automation.

options.title: Copy-only mitigation
options.body: Only replace the remaining sandbox error text and keep CLI-through-exec config mutation behavior unchanged, accepting that the deeper boundary remains open.

options.title: Accept current behavior
options.body: Document the current operator-powerful behavior and keep actionable config hints visible, leaving this report open only if a concrete current-main auto-writer is reproduced.

recommendation.title: Harden the mutation boundary
recommendation.body: Remove config-write assignments from assistant-visible errors, keep operator-only guidance in explicit CLI/status surfaces, and require audited operator provenance or denial for protected config writes reached through exec/cron automation.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior gateway config guard work is the closest existing owner signal for the model-to-operator config mutation boundary.
